items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: I met Fats in Chicago once, and I used to idolize him. ... They'd say, 'Mr. Jones, who was your teacher?' Well, I would start as far back as James P. Johnston and Fats Waller ... All these guys are my teachers, you know?

ctx.x: Well, it was the club, really, mainly. Maybe Connie's Inn or the Cotton Club or something like that, you know. And they would pick out the one that had the best shot, you know, picture, that is. But she would play the straight lady onstage, like at the Apollo, uptown, and the Alhambra, in those days, you know. And the old timers like Pigmeat, Pigmeat Markham, Dusty Fletcher. Gee whiz, I can't think of the rest of them. Maybe she did some work with (inaudible), too. But she knew Bert Williams. She never worked…

Duke?" And I said, "No, I'll meet him on my own terms, because she was going to invite him to dinner, because she knew him. Oh, she knew him that well, you know. And then when she moved to Pittsburgh, she had married the editor of the Pittsburgh Courier at that time, and she lived on the same -- oh, in the same apartment building with Lena, you know, the upstairs and downstairs. She used to nurse Lena's son, young Teddy that died, you know? And they knew -- they used to dance together. They knew each other very…
